kernel_of_truth.in_the_original_metaphor: The '1/0 as a finite number' framing was rhetorically attackable but it was capturing a real mathematical claim: if the dome treats κ as a single structural coefficient of the cavity, and the cavity's gravity response at later eclipses is 0 µGal at SG precision while the cavity's gravity response at the originating eclipse was 6.5 µGal at spring-gravimeter precision, then the dome's own data forces the denominator of κ to take two values simultaneously. There is no smooth functional resolution that makes 6.5 µGal and 0 µGal both the 'gravity response of the dome cavity during eclipse' under a single κ. The denominator does collapse on the dome's own later data — the metaphor was technically loose because the dome literally computed κ from the non-zero pair before the null measurements arrived, but the structural problem is real and survives any defender complaint about 'we did not divide by zero.'
kernel_of_truth.in_the_softened_framing: Reframing as 'denominator contradicted by later high-precision confirmations' makes the argument forward-defensible against the divide-by-zero literalism objection while keeping the bite: the dome lists Membach 1999 and China 2009 as confirmations, our review lists them as Refuted by Data, and BOTH classifications require that the eclipse gravity perturbation at those stations is 0 µGal. The dome cannot simultaneously cite 6.5 µGal and 0 µGal as 'the' cavity gravity response without publishing a station-discrimination rule — which would constitute new model surface area subject to falsification at every subsequent eclipse, and would also threaten PRED-TIER-3 if the August 2026 station happens to fall on the 'null' side of that rule.

why_softening_keeps_the_argument: Three substantive points are preserved unchanged: (1) the κ derivation uses non-replicated 1997 data as its denominator; (2) the dome's own later high-precision SG nulls contradict that denominator value; (3) the marquee forward prediction (PRED-TIER-3, August 2026 gravity perturbation) inherits the contradiction. The only thing dropped is the rhetorical compression 'treating 1/0 as a finite number,' which a defender can correctly point out is not what the dome literally did (the dome computed κ from a non-zero pair, then claimed later nulls as confirmations of the same model). The softened framing — 'denominator contradicted by the dome's own later high-precision confirmations cannot be treated as a fixed structural coefficient at the precision the dome itself cites' — survives this objection because it states exactly what the dome did and exactly why it is incoherent.
corrected_replacement_html_block:
2.13 The κ Coupling Constant: Denominator Contradicted by the Dome's Own Later Data

The dome's structural coupling constant κ = 1.67 nT/µGal is computed as a ratio of two numbers — magnetic perturbation (BOU 2017) divided by gravity perturbation (Mohe 1997). The dome's own subsequent eclipse data (WIN-013 Membach 1999, WIN-014 China 2009) report zero µGal at superconducting-gravimeter precision. A coupling constant whose denominator is the dome's own later null measurement cannot carry the precision the dome itself cites — and this same κ is the coefficient that drives the dome's marquee August 2026 eclipse prediction (PRED-TIER-3).

The structural problem. κ is the dome's own published magnetic-gravity coupling, derived from a single eclipse pair: −10.9 nT (BOU magnetometer, 2017 North-American eclipse, ~92% local coverage) divided by −6.5 µGal (Mohe spring gravimeter, March 1997 eclipse, Wuhan-region observation). The ratio is 1.67 nT/µGal — a number the dome carries forward as a fundamental geometric coefficient and uses to predict future eclipse signatures.

The dome's own later data nullifies the denominator. Both WIN-013 (1999 Membach total eclipse, superconducting-gravimeter null at 0.01–0.1 µGal precision) and WIN-014 (2009 East-Asian eclipse, Chinese SG network null at comparable precision) are listed by the dome as confirmations of cavity behavior; our review verdicts on the same data points are both Refuted by Data — the dome and the review agree that the gravimeter signal is null, and disagree about what that null means. The dome simultaneously claims (WIN-012) that the eclipse gravity perturbation is 6.5 µGal and (WIN-013/014) that the eclipse gravity perturbation is 0 µGal — at higher-precision instruments at longer-duration events. A coupling constant whose denominator is contradicted by the dome's own later high-precision confirmations cannot be treated as a fixed structural coefficient at the precision the dome itself cites; either κ is location-dependent (a model property the dome has not published), or one of the two denominator values is wrong, and the dome owes a stated rule for which.

The retreat to "spatial heterogeneity" reopens the wound elsewhere. A defender will say: κ applies only where the dome predicts a signal, and WIN-013/014 are at "non-discriminating" locations. But the dome never publishes a discrimination rule. If κ is a real coupling constant of the cavity, it should not turn off and on depending on station latitude. If it does turn off and on, the dome owes a stated location-dependent function — which would constitute new model surface area subject to its own subsequent falsification at each new eclipse. And critically: if κ can be "off" at Membach 1999 and "on" at BOU 2017, then κ can also be "off" at the August 2026 prediction site — destroying PRED-TIER-3, the dome's marquee forward eclipse claim. The defense saves the past at the cost of the future.

Why this is a self-contradiction, not a fitting failure. The standard external complaint against κ is that the two data points used in its derivation are from different events, different locations, different instruments, and one of them (Mohe 1997) has not been independently replicated. That criticism is valid but external. The criticism here is internal: the dome's own later confirmations contain a contradiction with the denominator of its own foundational constant. No external instrument is required — only the dome's own published WIN-012/013/014 numbers compared against each other. The 6.5 µGal denominator and the 0.0 µGal confirmations cannot both be true at the precision the dome itself cites. Tier-1 attack: the foundational coefficient of the dome's forward gravity prediction is invalidated by the dome's own later success-list. See WIN-012, WIN-013, WIN-014, and Part 6.14 κ Coupling Cluster cross-eclipse argument for the full derivation chain.

anticipated_objections.objection: Defender: 'You softened your own argument — you used to say divide-by-zero, now you say merely contradicted. You concede the original was wrong.'
anticipated_objections.response: The substantive claim has not moved: 6.5 µGal and 0 µGal are still the same coupling's denominator on the dome's own data, the contradiction is still internal to the dome's ledger, and PRED-TIER-3 still inherits the problem. What was softened is the rhetorical packaging — a metaphor that compressed 'the denominator value goes to zero in later data' into '1/0' was technically loose because the dome computed κ from a non-zero pair before the nulls arrived. The corrected wording states what the dome literally did and shows why it is incoherent at the precision the dome itself cites. Sharpening rhetoric while preserving substance is the same discipline we apply to the dome model — it is not a concession of error.

anticipated_objections.objection: Defender: 'WIN-013/014 are listed as confirmations because they are confirmations — the dome predicted no signal except at specific cavity-resonance conditions, and the SG nulls are consistent with that prediction.'
anticipated_objections.response: The dome publishes no such conditional rule in monitor.py or model.html — κ is presented as a structural cavity coefficient that produces 1.67 nT of magnetic response per 1 µGal of gravity response. There is no location-dependent function, no station-discrimination rule, no published mechanism by which the cavity 'turns off' at Membach but 'on' at BOU. The defender's framing requires new model surface area that does not exist in the dome's published material. If the dome adds such a rule post-hoc, that rule itself becomes a falsifiable claim at every subsequent eclipse — and PRED-TIER-3 immediately requires the dome to commit to which side of the rule the August 2026 site falls on, before the event.

anticipated_objections.objection: Defender: 'BOU 2017 and Mohe 1997 used different instrument types (proton magnetometer vs. spring gravimeter); the precision is not directly comparable to Membach 1999 / China 2009 SG networks.'
anticipated_objections.response: Conceded — and this is exactly the point. The dome's denominator (6.5 µGal from Mohe 1997 spring gravimeter) is by the dome's own listing of WIN-013/014 invalidated at higher precision. A coupling constant cited to two significant figures (1.67 nT/µGal) cannot survive a denominator whose nominal value is contradicted by a factor of >100 in precision-improved follow-up measurements. The dome's own confirmations of WIN-013/014 are precisely the act of accepting that improved-precision result — at which point the original denominator's two-significant-figure precision is unsupported.
